checks.claim: Long-distance power lines run at 100,000 to 800,000 volts, because higher voltage needs less current and loses less power as heat
checks.why: Energy Education gives 100 kV to 800 kV for overhead lines; GAO says higher voltage means less current and lower losses.

checks.claim: A common pole transformer turns 7,200 volts into the 240 and 120 volts a house uses
checks.why: 7200 primary 120/240 secondary pole-mount units are standard listings; primaries vary.

checks.claim: About 5 percent of the electricity is lost in transmission and distribution in America

sources.title: EIA FAQ: How much electricity is lost in transmission and distribution?
